name: Hellenic Republic

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 128,900 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Low/high allow for the Natural Earth polygon vs official figure and inland water (surface area is a few % larger).

population.note: asOf 2025: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 10,413,962. Range allows for 2026 drift and census revisions.

activePersonnel.note: IISS as quoted: 131,650 active incl. conscripts. Low: CIA Factbook 2025 ~112,000.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 131,650 minus infantry P roles (40,000). Covers navy and air force personnel, armour/artillery/air-defence crews, logistics, staff, training and other support.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Greece 1940-41 (~500,000 from ~7.3 million, ~7%) with universal male conscription and a large trained reserve.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry brigades (M113/Leonidas/BMP-1/Marder). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Hellenic_Army)

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): Old M113/BMP-1 heavy.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts (12 months) with professional cadre.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry divisions on the islands and Evros, marines, paratroopers and raiders. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Hellenic_Army)

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts; special forces well trained.

count.note: Leopard 2A6HEL 170 + 2A4 183 + Leopard 1A5 501 + M48A5 390 + M60A3 100 = 1,344 (high); low drops M48/M60 largely in storage.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Leopard 2A6HEL modern; Leopard 1/M48 obsolete.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts with professional crews.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): M113 and Leonidas old.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts.

count.note: M270 36 + PzH 2000 24 + M109 420 + M110 145 + M114 266 + M101 413 = 1,304 (high); many towed guns in reserve.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly below): M109/M110/M114 old; PzH 2000 and M270 modern.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Conscripts.

count.note: Rafale 24 (18+6) + F-16 212 (113 Viper/39 Block 52+/60 Block 30/50) + Mirage 2000-5 24 (19+5) = ~260 listed; F-4E 16 counted under strike. Mid allows for retirements.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): Rafale and F-16V among the region's best; F-35 ordered.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army): High readiness after decades of Aegean intercepts.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.25 (obsolete, a generation behind) (slightly above): F-4E.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: Army: AH-64A/D 28 + OH-58D 60 + CH-47 25 + NH90 20 + UH-1H/AB-205 100 + AB-206 14 = 247; Air Force AS332 12; Navy S-70B/MH-60R and AB-212 ~20.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical): Old UH-1 core, AH-64 and MH-60R modern.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

training.note: Rubric training 0.5 (conscripts with basic training) (slightly above): Professional.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Mostly 1980s-90s frigates; FDI new.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional, constant Aegean patrols.

count.note: Missile boats 13 + gunboats 8 + patrol 6 + MCM 2 + landing ships ~5 = ~34.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.75 (among the era's best) (slightly below): Type 214 AIP modern.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

count.note: Air Force Patriot 6 squadrons + S-300PMU-1 1 + Crotale 9 systems; Army Hawk 7 batteries + Osa 7 batteries + Tor 21 systems (~4 per battery, ~5) + ASRAD 54 launchers (~6 per battery, ~9); 631 Stinger MANPADS not counted. ~40.

quality.note: Rubric quality 0.5 (era-typical) (slightly above): Patriot PAC-3 and old Soviet/Hawk systems.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75 (professional standing army) (slightly below): Professional.

commandQuality.note: Rubric commandQuality 0.5 (competent staff, average generalship) (slightly above): Competent NATO-integrated staff; no major combat since 1974.

cohesion.note: Rubric cohesion 0.75 (professional with strong unit identity) (slightly below): National conscript army with strong identity tied to the Turkish threat.

morale.note: Rubric morale 0.75 (motivated, recent victories) (slightly below): Motivated for national defence of islands and Evros.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: SCALP, Exocet, Meteor; Achilles Shield GBAD planned.

armor.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Leopard 2A6HEL; many Cold War tanks.

ships.note: Anchor 9: Type 214, FDI frigates new; rest old.

fortification.note: Anchor 9: Island fortifications and Evros fence; Patriot GBAD.

logistics.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Short interior lines, island resupply.

isr.note: Between anchor 8 and 9: Limited UAV ISR, Hellas Sat.

air.note: Between anchor 9 and 10: Rafale F3R, F-16V; F-35 from 2028.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 318,605,655,941 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 10,413,962 = 30,594. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 398,008,314,729 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 318,605,655,941 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 2.99% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 2.88% in 2024, 3.80% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 15.2% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Exporter of olive oil, fruit and fish; imports grain and meat.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 5,046,070 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.724% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 57,769. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Domestic yards assist FDI/Constellation work; most hulls built abroad. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Hellenic_Navy_ships)

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 2,339 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 53,459 thousand DWT under the Greek flag; Greek owners control the world's largest merchant fleet (~400 million DWT under all flags, educated reading of the same list), high.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. By analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment (truck-based, depots every ~150-200 km).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states. FAS lists the five US B61 host states (Belgium, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Turkey); this state is not one of them.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: mountains, fortified islands and Evros, strong population support.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:GRC. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from the Wikipedia Hellenic Army equipment list, active Greek military aircraft list and active Hellenic Navy ship list; drones = Group 2+ only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Large Cold War stocks in reserve make high/low spreads wide.
